title: Ordinary-flight Step Response is an estimate
summary: Airframe summarizes repeated setpoint-to-gyro behaviour from suitable flight windows; the curve is evidence about that recording, not a literal stick step or a one-term PID diagnosis.

blocks.text: Airframe divides setpoint and filtered gyro into overlapping two-second windows, rejects windows without enough excitation, applies a Hamming taper, performs regularized Wiener deconvolution, smooths and integrates the impulse estimate, then averages accepted responses over the first 500 ms.

blocks.caption: What the current result reports
rows: How much of the selected flight contributed to the estimate.
More windows do not make dissimilar manoeuvres comparable.
The highest value of the averaged unit-step estimate; values above 1 indicate the response exceeded the commanded level.
Peak alone does not identify P, D, Feedforward, filtering, or mechanics as the cause.
Time until the estimate first reaches half of its steady-state value.
Filtering, plant dynamics, control authority, and estimator quality all contribute.
Time between the first 10% and 90% crossings.
Unavailable crossings remain unavailable rather than being inferred.

blocks.title: The flight supplies the excitation
blocks.text: Manoeuvres, rates, battery state, props, payload, wind, filters, selected range, and accepted-window count can all change the estimate. Compare curves only when the evidence is reasonably comparable.
